title: Every written CST stamp is checked against the clock
why: Triage stamps ran 11-16 min ahead of now-central from about 09:50 to 09:57 CST Nov 13 (audit 10:01 CST). That covered the handoff header, a push time and a runner message. The message-time hook checks send_message only, and caught one at 10:00 CST. Handoff headers, step notes and page reply stamps are not checked. SLIPS 11:50 CST Nov 14 (triage, own): at 11:49 CST the clock read 11:49, but triage had stamped filings at 11:52 (script 1030) and 12:00 (script 1031), and sent messages dated 11:53, 11:54 and 12:01, by counting forward from an earlier hook line instead of reading ~/.claude/bin/now-central. The added time of items 836, 837 and 838 was corrected to 11:49. Records with the wrong stamps: the notes headed 11:52 and 12:00 on steps ci-wait-stop-needs-checkin, runner-ready-mark-check-in, combine-train-tool, ready-push-moves-linted-head, ci-batch-mac-runner, records-page-before-ready, record-after-each-round, and the plan Part 9 and 10 lines of that time; they are before 11:49, exact time unknown. Guard that would have stopped it: this step (stamp-clock-check-everywhere), still unstarted.
note: Fix: extend the message-time check (its one home) to handoff writes and roadmap step note stamps, with the same 1-minute limit. Done when: a test writes a handoff stamped 10 minutes ahead and is refused. Incident 11:11 CST Nov 13 (coordinator): batch runner 11 stamped a message 11:15 CST at 11:11 CST, 4 minutes ahead; a second session with the same drift. Incident 11:14 CST Nov 13 (coordinator): triage wrote "Routed at 11:16 CST" in a page thread reply at 11:14 CST, without reading now-central. Second incident (retrospective 11:38 CST Nov 13): from about 11:30 to 11:39 CST triage wrote stamps up to 68 minutes ahead of the clock (for example "12:46 CST" at 11:38 CST) in notes, rulings, page replies and chat headers, by estimating the time instead of reading now-central at the send. The retrospective's guard message-time-matches-clock refused that drift on its sends and let triage's through. Corrected in place 11:40 CST: 5 step and ruling notes, the outbox, 7 page items; chat headers already sent stay wrong. Triage reads now-central before every stamp; open question for the lane: does the guard run in this session? Second incident, 12:32 CST Nov 13 (coordinator 12:32 CST): from about 12:20 to 12:31 CST real time its message headers ran 7 to 12 minutes ahead (e.g. "12:43" sent at about 12:30), stamped from memory, not now-central. The header-time guard did not refuse them, though its record says it refuses over 1 minute of drift: possible gap (it may check only some message paths). Notes filed today that quote coordinator times from 12:20 on (the R9 broadcast "12:42", the 12:3x asks, mailbox ruling 12:37, #3177 12:38) carry those wrong clock times; real time is about 7 to 12 minutes earlier. Stood: two senders, same drift, same guard miss. Retro measure, 12:32 CST Nov 13 (retro 12:32 CST): the coordinator's stamps ran 10 to 15 minutes ahead, read at arrival: "12:37" arrived 12:27 CST, "12:42" arrived 12:29 CST. This is the retro's arrival read; the coordinator's own estimate was 7 to 12 minutes. Use the arrival read. Express lane started 12:43 CST Nov 13 (coordinator 12:44 CST): session_013NEJKzsL8rGwdtrXndbSsp. Three incidents on this step: triage, the coordinator, and the retro-measured 10 to 15 minute drift. Triage 20:07 CST Nov 13: carries the folded step no-future-time-stamps (the wrote-a-guessed-time guard). Open draft PR #3234, head 931c4f50808d (coordinator REST read 20:06). Gap from the folded lane (via the coordinator 20:09 CST Nov 13, read from diffs, unmeasured): #3234 does not cover (a) the record filer's fs_lib new and upd stamps, the script this triage session uses to file steps, and (b) a placeholder time of the form "<hh>:<m>x". Kept as a gap note; not a new step yet.
